page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized server instance from the c2d family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 cores with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU capabilities, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core benchmarks. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and general compute workloads fall consistently in the middle 50% tier. Specifically, memory bandwidth reaches 553.05 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 62.15 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as Passmark encryption and bzip3 decompression, also perform within the average range.

While the instance handles small-scale LLM inference efficiently, processing medium 7B models reveals a bottleneck, with prompt processing speeds dropping into the bottom 25% tier. This indicates a performance tradeoff for larger machine learning tasks. Given its high memory allocation relative to compute cores, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as database operations, web serving, software compilation, and moderate data processing tasks that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
